subject: Veridian PoC: post-demo recap, success criteria & SDK routing next steps

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood-inference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>

Subject: Veridian PoC: post-demo recap, success criteria & SDK routing next steps

Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our demo & discovery and proposed next steps to get a short PoC in motion:

What we heard (high level)
- Primary goal: reduce customer support deflection for chat workflows by 40% while keeping >95% classification accuracy on intent extraction.
- Non-functional: 200ms p95 for in-path generation, support 20 requests/sec sustained during peak window.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II evidence and audit logs required; data residency preference: us-east.

Proposed PoC success criteria (please confirm):
1) Functional: end-to-end conversation flow integrated with Veridian chat UI that reduces false-positive support transfers by >=40% on pilot dataset.
2) Quality: intent extraction F1 >= 0.95 on validation set supplied by Veridian.
3) Performance: generation p95 < 200ms for 512-token sessions; sustained throughput >= 20 rps, with graceful degradation fallback to lower-cost model if latency spikes.
4) Observability: request-level traces and token-level cost breakdown available in Redwood Console; daily latency and quality report.

Technical asks for kickoff / what we need from Veridian
- Sandbox dataset: ~5k representative conversations (anonymized) + schema (CSV or JSON).
- API keys / IP allowlist for Redwood test environment (we can use hosted staging or a dedicated trial cluster).
- Security checklist answers (SOC2 report, data retention policy, encryption requirements).

Initial PoC timeline (approx)
- Week 0 (this week): confirm success criteria, exchange NDA if needed, share dataset sample.
- Week 1: Redwood provisioning + SDK handoff; smoke test on sample data.
- Week 2–3: Integration + metrics baseline collection.
- Week 4: Acceptance review and next-phase decision.

Ownership & suggested participants
- Veridian: Samir (product), Elena (engineering), Legal (contract).
- Redwood: Priyom (sales/eng lead), Ben (solutions & SDK owner), Marissa (CS / success).

Ben, Marissa — can you review the tech asks below and confirm owner assignments?

Attachments: PoC-MAP-v1.pdf (PoC milestones + acceptance checklist), veridian-sample-schema.csv (example rows)

Next steps
- Samir: confirm the success criteria above and share dataset sample + legal contact.
- Redwood: prepare trial cluster options (hosted vs dedicated) and SDK routing plan; propose kickoff slots.

Thanks —

Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri.yom@redwood-inference.com | +1 415-555-0132

Priyom —

Thanks for the clear notes. Quick confirmations and a couple additions from our side:

- Success criteria: Agree with the four bullets; we would add a cost target for the pilot: average per-conversation inference spend < $0.015. If Redwood has suggestions for model/quantization mixes to meet this, share recommendations.
- Performance: 200ms p95 is ideal; if we need to relax during early experiments that’s okay as long as the baseline is tracked.
- Data: we can provide a 2k-row anonymized sample by EOD tomorrow and the full 5k set by Tuesday (we will scrub PII).
- Compliance: Legal needs SOC 2 Type II report and a basic data processing addendum (DPA). I’ve looped Legal on this thread.

On environment: we prefer starting on your hosted trial (so teams can iterate quickly), but if dedicated capacity is recommended for reliability we’re open — request a quote for both.

Kickoff availability: Tue 21 Jul 10–12 PDT or Wed 22 Jul 13–16 PDT.

Samir
Samir Patel

samir@veridian.ai

Priyom / Marissa —

Notes from the engineering/SDK side and proposed implementation plan:

1) Trial environment choice- If Veridian wants fast iteration we should run on hosted trial initially. We can spin a sandbox project with per-route quotas and streaming enabled. Dedicated capacity quote should include a reserved pool for peak windows and an SLA. I will ask infra for a rough TCO estimate.

2) SDK / API routing- Primary integration: Redwood Streaming API for live chat to keep UI latency low (we stream deltas and tokens). Use SDK v2 (node/python) and the streaming client; provide a simple example that wires Redwood's streaming -> Veridian websocket.
- Fallback: model-variant routing policy (low-cost quantized variant) when p95 > 250ms for a configurable window.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and deterministic completion seeds to cut token counts.

3) Tool calling & structured outputs- For intent extraction and tool triggers (e.g., escalate_to_agent), we recommend function-calling style structured responses (JSON schema) and a post-processing hook in Veridian code. We'll provide example schemas and mapping.

4) Telemetry & instrumentation- Instrument token-level cost, request IDs, and traces into the Redwood Console. Add a daily job to compute baseline metrics and emit a weekly report to the Veridian Slack channel (or email).

5) Owners & timeline- Ben: SDK examples / streaming sample (deliverable: github repo + README) — target Thu 23 Jul.
- Marissa: onboarding playbook & acceptance checklist — target Fri 24 Jul.
- Priyom: coordinate dataset & legal (ongoing).

6) Risks / blockers- SOC 2 paperwork may delay dedicated cluster provisioning. If Legal needs additional doc signing, expedite DPA template.

I’ll draft the sample code and a small routing policy yaml. Priyom — I can be on the kickoff Tue/Wed as needed.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
